title: Sonne Finance — donation into an empty market inflates the soToken exchange rate

ground_truth.description: Sonne Finance, a Compound V2 fork, was exploited on Optimism on 14 May 2024 for roughly $20M because a market's share price is derived from the balance the contract happens to hold rather than from what was deposited. exchangeRateStoredInternal() computes (getCashPrior() + totalBorrows - totalReserves) / totalSupply, so underlying tokens transferred directly to the market raise totalCash without minting any shares and inflate the exchange rate; mintFresh() and redeemFresh() then divide by that rate with truncating integer division (mintTokens = actualMintAmount / exchangeRate, redeemTokens = redeemAmountIn / exchangeRate), so the rounded-away remainder is left behind for whoever already holds shares. A newly listed soVELO market was created and configured in separate timelocked, permissionlessly executable transactions, which left a window in which the market existed with an essentially empty supply. The attacker minted a dust soVELO position, donated a flash-loaned ~35.5M VELO straight to the soVELO contract, and drove the exchange rate high enough that 1 wei of soVELO carried millions of tokens of collateral value — enough to borrow roughly 265 WETH against it. Repeating the borrow across the Optimism markets and then redeeming the dust position to recover the donation drained about $20M in WETH, USDC.e and VELO.
